chunks.heading: Dream Journal
chunks.notes: This chunk is the frontmatter-style note listing the six entry titles and source provenance, not narrative content itself.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: The dream opens with the narrator both painting and "hovering just outside my own body" as witness to himself, a doubled-self opening image.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: Introduces "another version of me...older, steadier" as teacher, an explicit double-self figure.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: Closes the first vision (child-self and future-artist-self meeting, gratitude/covenant language) then "V. 2" restarts the same dream-territory from scratch.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: The subconscious speaks directly ("Hey. I got this.") while the observer-self watches the artist-self, the entry's peak moment of self-recognition and covenant-forming.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: Formally introduces the "Elder-Artist" double and returns to childhood loneliness reframed as companionship via imagination.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: A repeated "To ___" vow-list structure delivered as the dream "asked for a vow" at its threshold moment.

chunks.heading: The Night I Became the Artist
chunks.notes: Closes the entry with explicit aphorisms ("Art isn't something I do. It's the way my soul breathes").

chunks.heading: THE NIGHT I GOT IN HIS TRUCK
chunks.notes: Opens a new entry with the narrator approaching Kanye and stating his hope to "follow a path like his."

chunks.heading: THE NIGHT I GOT IN HIS TRUCK
chunks.notes: The truck-singing scene builds to Kanye's line "we're gonna make you a star," felt as "destiny snapping into place."

chunks.heading: THE NIGHT I GOT IN HIS TRUCK
chunks.notes: The house dissolves from a singing scene into a cluttered, decaying room -- "broken objects, forgotten things, pieces of a life left unattended."

chunks.heading: THE NIGHT I GOT IN HIS TRUCK
chunks.notes: The narrator recognizes the messy house as a mirror of his own neglected mind and resolves to "take control."

chunks.heading: The Fragile Versions of Us
chunks.notes: Opens on a liminal Kansas landscape where the narrator feels "suspended between versions of myself," beside a woman who has already judged him.

chunks.heading: The Fragile Versions of Us
chunks.notes: A cruel remark lands but the narrator responds by calmly walking away rather than pleading to be seen differently.

chunks.heading: The Fragile Versions of Us
chunks.notes: Confronting Katie directly names past rejection as "a mistake, a fault," and the narrator acknowledges he "had almost ended my life because of her rejection."

chunks.heading: The Fragile Versions of Us
chunks.notes: The scene dissolves into remembered youth with Ella, recalling mutual immaturity and unspoken hurt.

chunks.heading: The Fragile Versions of Us
chunks.notes: The entry closes on readiness for a future partner "in artistry, depth, nature, and spirit" rather than a resolved conversation.

chunks.heading: The Fragile Versions of Us
chunks.notes: A single closing line, "And then I woke," with no further content to tag.

chunks.heading: Where the Light Pauses
chunks.notes: Opens in a church with a dying homeless man, and the narrator "couldn't tell if I was meant to witness the moment or be swallowed by it."

chunks.heading: Where the Light Pauses
chunks.notes: A son watches his father's stilled breath, then the scene "pans through a doorway" to a mother beside a dead loved one.

chunks.heading: Where the Light Pauses
chunks.notes: A little girl watches from a doorway as the hallway lengthens into a corridor where the church/street/bedroom scenes bleed together.

chunks.heading: Where the Light Pauses
chunks.notes: Closes on the aphorism that "the beauty in defeat isn't the fall, but the pause after," as the dream releases the narrator.

chunks.heading: The Storm and the Buoy
chunks.notes: Opens with the narrator clinging to a buoy in a storm while "a nasty voice grew inside me telling me to let go."

chunks.heading: The Storm and the Buoy
chunks.notes: Showing family something he made, he's met with indifference and the reductive line "how are you gonna make money."

chunks.heading: The Storm and the Buoy
chunks.notes: Back on the buoy, the narrator rises and stands "on top of the ocean" instead of clinging, framed as having "taken my life into my own hands."

chunks.heading: The Couch and the Breath
chunks.notes: Opens the dated entry with an unhurried intimate scene where the narrator takes pride in noticing Mya's involuntary breath change.

chunks.heading: The Couch and the Breath
chunks.notes: The narrator names his orientation as wanting "to give... not perform," and distinguishes the felt difference between sex and love.

chunks.heading: The Couch and the Breath
chunks.notes: A juxtaposed image is immediately re-narrated in explicit terms via the Jungian anima figure "wearing Mya's face."

chunks.heading: The Couch and the Breath
chunks.notes: Closes the entry (and file) on the realization that "the work isn't learning it. The work is clearing away everything that makes me forget."
